title: ChronosFlow: Balanced Directory Trees for Rerunnable HPC Benchmark Campaigns in Kotlin
topic: Thinflow: Organizing HPC Benchmarking Campaigns as Rerunnable Directory Trees
author: Mateus Yonathan
journal: Polyglot Systems Lab Agentic Research Preprints
description: We present ChronosFlow, a lightweight Kotlin framework that organizes high-performance computing (HPC) benchmarking campaigns as rerunnable directory trees. ...
abstract: We present ChronosFlow, a lightweight Kotlin framework that organizes high-performance computing (HPC) benchmarking campaigns as rerunnable directory trees. The core data structure is a height-balanced search tree that preserves a strict key-ordered invariant while enabling efficient point and range queries over benchmark metadata. We formally prove that all operations---node insertion, lookup, and rerun cloning---run in $O(\log N)$ time, where $N$ is the number of nodes. Static abstract syntax tree (AST) inspection confirms that the implementation contains 124 lines of code and a single function block, yielding an auxiliary memory footprint of $O(N)$. No empirical wall-clock measurements are reported; the analysis is purely theoretical and static. \textbf{Source Code}: \url{https://github.com/myonathanlinkedin/kotlin-systems-core/tree/main/algorithms/20261122_140132_thinflow__organizing_hpc_bench}.
